predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Russian Republic row (1917-1919) also covers Belarus in 1918; the corps was a Russian army corps formed at Minsk on 24 July 1917 and refused the Soviet order to disband on 25 January 1918.

successors.note: The corps agreed on 21 May 1918 'to be disarmed and disbanded' with the Germans; the Brest-Litovsk treaty 'gave all of Poland and Belarus to Germany'. The units 'retreated to Poland'.

capitals.name: Babruysk
capitals.note: Headquarters of the occupied districts after 28 February 1918; the corps was formed in Minsk on 24 July 1917 and withdrew from Minsk to Babruysk on 31 January 1918.

rulers.title: corps commander
rulers.note: Appointed commander on 6 August 1917 (the page elsewhere gives 23 August Old Style); on 21 May 1918 he signed the agreement that disbanded the corps.

keyframe_review.note: 50,817 km2 (231 cells) as a north-south ribbon of Belarus at 27.8-29.9 E, 51.4-56.2 N (Mozyr to Vitebsk); the gazetteer finds Babruysk and Mozyr inside but not Zhlobin, Slutsk or Mogilev. The page puts the corps in '6 Belarusian districts in the triangle of Mogilev-Zhlobin-Slutsk, with their headquarters at Babruysk' after 28 February 1918, and gives no area, so the shape cannot be checked against it (page silent); the triangle drawn from the three towns is about 8,000 km2 (researcher's estimate from the coordinates) and the six districts more, so the Cliopatria shape is probably too large and too far north and south. Cliopatria labels the row with the modern 'Polish Land Forces' article (infobox 'Founded: 1918'), which does not mention the corps.

region.text: '6 Belarusian districts in the triangle of Mogilev-Zhlobin-Slutsk, with their headquarters at Babruysk'

ledger.note: 1918, February-March: the I Polish Corps holds six Belarusian districts. The corps (formed in Minsk on 24 July 1917, nearly 30,000 men in January 1918) 'occupied 6 Belarusian districts in the triangle of Mogilev-Zhlobin-Slutsk, with their headquarters at Babruysk' after 28 February 1918; it had refused a Soviet order to disband on 25 January and joined the German offensive of 18 February, Minsk being taken on 21 February.

region.text: the Babruysk fortress and its district

ledger.note: 1918, 2 February: the siege of the Babruysk fortress begins. After refusing to disband the corps retreated 'from Minsk to Babruysk' on 31 January; 'on 2 February the siege of the Babruysk fortress began'.

region.text: the Babruysk fortress and its district

ledger.note: 1918, 11 March: the Babruysk fortress falls ('the fortress fell on 11 March, but the German army forced the Polish forces to give over the fortress').

region.text: '6 Belarusian districts in the triangle of Mogilev-Zhlobin-Slutsk, with their headquarters at Babruysk'

ledger.note: 1918, 21 May: the corps is disbanded. 'On 21 May 1918, Dowbor-Musnicki signed an agreement with the Germans, under which the Corps agreed to be disarmed and disbanded'; the units retreated to Poland. The page gives no exact dissolution date.

wars.name: I Polish Corps in Russia: refusal to disband and the Babruysk operations

zones.text: the Babruysk fortress and its district

wars.outcome: The corps refused the Soviet disbandment order on 25 January 1918, fought around Babruysk from 2 February, joined the German offensive of 18 February (Minsk on 21 February), held six districts from 28 February and was disarmed by the Germans after the agreement of 21 May 1918.
wars.note: The corps was a Russian-army formation of Polish soldiers, not a state; the page does not call it a rebel force.

certainty.note: A military occupation of districts; no treaty or survey line; the page names the triangle by three towns.

notes: Page budget 2 of 2. Cliopatria row 'Polish Armed Forces' (1918, Q248989, Wikipedia 'Polish Land Forces') is not a state: the shape is the territory of the I Polish Corps in Russia of Dowbor-Musnicki in Belarus, identified by the 'Mogilev-Zhlobin-Slutsk triangle, headquarters Babruysk' of the corps page; the Land Forces page does not mention it. Typed 'rebel' (armed formation holding land, hatched until disbanded) as the nearest of the schema's types; the orchestrator may prefer to drop the row or type it 'umbrella'. Page silent: the corps' area, the exact dissolution day, the German military administration of the districts afterwards, the Belarusian People's Republic of 25 March 1918 and the other Polish formations (II and III Corps, Polish Legions). Counterpart russian-soviet-federative-socialist-republic is the Soviet side (Cliopatria's Russian Republic row 1917..1919 covers the same land); german-empire has no Cliopatria shape over Belarus in 1918. Date ambiguity: the corps commander's appointment is 6 August 1917 (page) or 23 August Old Style (page, elsewhere); the corps formed on 24 July 1917 (not 11 June).
